brief: Goldman's TMT sales desk wraps Day 1 of the Communacopia and Technology Conference. Across OpenAI, Alphabet, SAP, Snowflake and Databricks the debate has moved from model capability to cost per task, governance and model choice, so enterprises are buying model-agnostic platforms that route work to the cheapest adequate model, which is why SAP expects agents to run on Mistral and open-source models and Databricks built the Unity AI Gateway. OpenAI reports 25m agentic users and roughly 1bn consumer users, rising revenue per GPU and falling unit costs, and expects pricing to move from seats to consumption to outcomes. On infrastructure, Broadcom, Arista, Infineon and Nebius report strong demand and better visibility, with the binding constraint now supply, power, permitting and data-centre construction rather than end demand. Broadcom reaffirms FY27 and FY28 AI revenue targets of $115bn and $230bn. Visa reports US payment volume growth of 6-8% and cross-border volumes up 14%. The desk flags that this is Day 1 only, that investors will debate SAP's multiple after the bounce, and that debate over personal agents Instinct and Meta Muse knocked online travel names.
